Variable Bit Rate Color Compression with Macro Blocks is a compression format for sparse 3D color data that uses variable bits per weight (bpw) to optimize compression ratio, addressing the limitation of fixed bpw methods where theoretical optimal compression is constrained by header overhead [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly describes a compression format for sparse 3D color data that uses variable bits per weight (bpw) to optimize compression ratio. It addresses the limitation of fixed bpw methods (specifically mentioning the theoretical optimal compression constraint due to header overhead). It details the use of 'macro blocks' (segregating the color array into smaller sets, specifically 2^14 colors) and explains the mechanism of using variable bpw (1-4 bpw plus a sentinel) to reduce header overhead compared to fixed methods.
